action: Fandango's notice urges recipients to review account statements, promptly report unauthorized transactions to their card issuer or bank, and activate the free IDX monitoring it offers by February 13, 2027.
date_note: Day of BleepingComputer's and eSecurityPlanet's reports; the notice template read on oag.ca.gov gives no date of its own. Exposure window 8-11 October 2026.
exec: Card data was captured at checkout on a major ticketing site, creating fraud exposure for customers and liability for the company.
plain: Ticket seller Fandango is telling customers that someone could access card details typed into its checkout page from October 8-11, 2026. It has not said how many people are affected.

sources.name: Fandango notice of data breach (California Attorney General)

summary: Fandango's notice, filed with the California Attorney General, says an unauthorized party could access payment card information for certain checkout-page transactions from October 8-11, 2026: card number, CVV, expiry, billing ZIP and email, not names, ID or SSNs. It determined this on October 30 and knows of no fraudulent use. BleepingComputer reported card-skimming code; the notice does not name the method or a count.
title: Fandango notice: unauthorized party could access payment card details on its checkout page

validation.note: Follow-up 22 Nov: Fandango's own notice template on oag.ca.gov read in full (primary); eSecurityPlanet (16 Nov) also read. The notice does not describe the method; card skimming is BleepingComputer's report. eSecurityPlanet cites SecurityWeek for Oregon and Vermont filing counts; SecurityWeek answered 403, so those counts are not used.

review.note: BleepingComputer read in full: summary lacked facts; now states skimmer on checkout page, Oct 8-11 exposure, data types, Oct 30 determination, no count disclosed
